answers.core: Communication of fundamental types to the browser cannot possibly be achieved by an add-on.
answers.workaround:
This is certainly an infrequent use case.  But there is no way to work around this.  It could be possible to encode your data as a string, but if your string contains any `\0` bytes, then that will be understood during Javascript decoding as a terminator, which would cause all the remaining data to be ignored.
You could also send your data one byte or int at a time, but this would be incredibly slow.
